card.name: Comma after dose schedule before frequency limit
card.fires_on: The comma or short unit word that ends a dose or increment phrase, just before a qualifier such as 'as needed' or 'no more frequently than'. Seen mainly in dosing instructions.

modes.label: Comma after dose phrase
modes.description: A comma ends a clause about a dose or titration step, before a limit on how often or when.
modes.example: subsequent treatment courses of 12 mg per day on 3 consecutive days (36 mg total dose) may be administered<<,>> as needed, at least 12

modes.label: Unit word ending an increment
modes.description: The word day, /day or hours closes an increment phrase such as 'in increments of 50 mg'.
modes.example: Dose increases should be in increments of up to 75 mg per<< day>>, as needed, and should be made

modes.label: Non-drug comma
modes.description: A comma after a clause with 'or' alternatives in general text.
modes.example: and two red spaces<<,>> or it could simply mean four black spaces
